entries.db347ee03edc4146cf9364b6bbdba13763e86c6d: <div sID="gen4459" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="19" osisID="Josh.19" sID="Josh.19"/> <div eID="gen4459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4460" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen4461" type="x-p"/> In the description of the lots of Judah and Benjamin we have an account both of the borders that surrounded them and of the cities contained in them. In that of Ephraim and Manasseh we have the borders, but not the cities; in this chapter Simeon and Dan are described by their cities only, and not their borders, because they lay very much within Judah, especially the former; the rest have both their borders described and their cities names, especially frontiers. Here is, I. The lot of Simeon, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.1-Josh.19.9">ver. 1-9</reference>. II. Of Zebulun, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.10-Josh.19.16">ver. 10-16</reference>. III. Of Issachar, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.17-Josh.19.23">ver. 17-23</reference>. IV. Of Asher, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.24-Josh.19.31">ver. 24-31</reference>. V. Of Naphtali, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.32-Josh.19.39">ver. 32-39</reference>. VI. Of Dan, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.40-Josh.19.48">ver. 40-48</reference>. Lastly, The inheritance assigned to Joshua himself and his own family, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.49-Josh.19.51">ver. 49-51</reference>.
entries.c9034c443b2d17370d0ea66ca459915a645d77d3: <div eID="gen4461" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen4460" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Lot of Simeon. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4462" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And the second lot came forth to Simeon, <hi type="italic">even</hi> for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families: and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah. <hi type="super">2</hi> And they had in their inheritance Beer-sheba, or Sheba, and Moladah, <hi type="super">3</hi> And Hazar-shual, and Balah, and Azem, <hi type="super">4</hi> And Eltolad, and Bethul, and Hormah, <hi type="super">5</hi> And Ziklag, and Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah, <hi type="super">6</hi> And Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities and their villages: <hi type="super">7</hi> Ain, Remmon, and Ether, and Ashan; four cities and their villages: <hi type="super">8</hi> And all the villages that <hi type="italic">were</hi> round about these cities to Baalath-beer, Ramath of the south. This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families. <hi type="super">9</hi> Out of the portion of the children of Judah <hi type="italic">was</hi> the inheritance of the children of Simeon: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them. <div eID="gen4462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4463" type="x-p"/> Simeon's lot was drawn after Judah's, Joseph's, and Benjamin's, because Jacob had put that tribe under disgrace; yet it is put before the two younger sons of Leah and the three sons of the handmaids. Not one person of note, neither judge nor prophet, was of this tribe, that we know of. <div eID="gen4463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4464" type="x-p"/> I. The situation of their lot was within that of Judah (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.1">v. 1</reference>) and was taken from it, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.9">v. 9</reference>. It seems, those that first surveyed the land thought it larger than it was, and that it would have held out to give every tribe in proportion as large a share as they had carved out for Judah; but, upon a more strict enquiry, it was found that it would not reach (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.9">v. 9</reference>): <hi type="italic">The part of the children of Judah was too much for them,</hi> more than they needed, and more, as it proved, than fell to their share. Yet God did not by the lot lessen it, but left it to their prudence and care afterwards to discover and rectify the mistake, which when they did, 1. The men of Judah did not oppose the taking away of the cities again, which by the first distribution fell within their border, when they were convinced that they had more than their proportion. In all such cases errors must be excepted and a review admitted if there be occasion. Though, in strictness, what fell to their lot was their right against all the world, yet they would not insist upon it when it appeared that another tribe would want what they had to spare. Note, We must look on the things of others, and not on our own only. The abundance of some must supply the wants of others, that there may be somewhat of an equality, for which there may be equity where there is not law. 2. That which was thus taken off from Judah to be put into a new lot Providence directed to the tribe of Simeon, that Jacob's prophecy concerning this tribe might be fulfilled, <hi type="italic">I will divide them in Jacob.</hi> The cities of Simeon were scattered in Judah, with which tribe they were surrounded, except on that side towards the sea. This brought them into a confederacy with the tribe of Judah (<reference osisRef="Judg.1.3">Judg. i. 3</reference>), and afterwards was a happy occasion of the adherence of many of this tribe to the house of David, at the time of the revolt of the ten tribes to Jeroboam. <reference osisRef="2Chr.15.9">2 Chron. xv. 9</reference>, <hi type="italic">out of Simeon they fell to</hi> Asa <hi type="italic">in abundance.</hi> It is good being in a good neighbourhood. <div eID="gen4464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4465" type="x-p"/> II. The cities within their lot are here named. Beersheba, or Sheba, for these names seem to refer to the same place, is put first. Ziklag, which we read of in David's story, is one of them. What course they took to enlarge their borders and make room for themselves we find <reference osisRef="1Chr.4.39-1Chr.4.43">1 Chron. iv. 39</reference>, &c.
entries.d6f5dae3e0b378bbd7c4c85476711a1e1544ae3a: <div eID="gen4465" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Lot of Zebulun. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4466" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">10</hi> And the third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families: and the border of their inheritance was unto Sarid: <hi type="super">11</hi> And their border went up toward the sea, and Maralah, and reached to Dabbasheth, and reached to the river that <hi type="italic">is</hi> before Jokneam; <hi type="super">12</hi> And turned from Sarid eastward toward the sunrising unto the border of Chisloth-tabor, and then goeth out to Daberath, and goeth up to Japhia, <hi type="super">13</hi> And from thence passeth on along on the east to Gittah-hepher, to Ittah-kazin, and goeth out to Remmon-methoar to Neah; <hi type="super">14</hi> And the border compasseth it on the north side to Hannathon: and the outgoings thereof are in the valley of Jiphthah-el: <hi type="super">15</hi> And Kattath, and Nahallal, and Shimron, and Idalah, and Beth-lehem: twelve cities with their villages. <hi type="super">16</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families, these cities with their villages. <div eID="gen4466" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4467" type="x-p"/> This is the lot of Zebulun, who, though born of Leah after Issachar, yet was blessed by Jacob and Moses before him; and therefore it was so ordered that his lot was drawn before that of Issachar, north of which it lay and south of Asher. 1. The lot of this tribe was washed by the great sea on the west, and by the sea of Tiberias on the east, answering Jacob's prophecy (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.13">Gen. xlix. 13</reference>), <hi type="italic">Zebulun shall be a haven of ships,</hi> trading ships on the great sea and fishing ships on the sea of Galilee. 2. Though there were some places in this tribe which were made famous in the Old Testament, especially <hi type="italic">Mount Carmel,</hi> on which the famous trial was between God and Baal in Elijah's time, yet it was made much more illustrious in the New Testament; for within the lot of this tribe was Nazareth, where our blessed Saviour spent so much of his time on earth, and from which he was called <hi type="italic">Jesus of Nazareth,</hi> and <hi type="italic">Mount Tabor</hi> on which he was transfigured, and that coast of the sea of Galilee on which Christ preached so many sermons and wrought so many miracles.
entries.7869e8ee2b5a0fa02f76e68aca5105cd8463c7c1: <div eID="gen4467" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Lot of Issachar. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4468" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">17</hi> <hi type="italic">And</hi> the fourth lot came out to Issachar, for the children of Issachar according to their families. <hi type="super">18</hi> And their border was toward Jezreel, and Chesulloth, and Shunem, <hi type="super">19</hi> And Hapharaim, and Shion, and Anaharath, <hi type="super">20</hi> And Rabbith, and Kishion, and Abez, <hi type="super">21</hi> And Remeth, and En-gannim, and En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez; <hi type="super">22</hi> And the coast reacheth to Tabor, and Shahazimah, and Beth-shemesh; and the outgoings of their border were at Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages. <hi type="super">23</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities and their villages. <div eID="gen4468" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4469" type="x-p"/> The lot of Issachar ran from Jordan in the east to the great sea in the west, Manasseh on the south, and Zebulun on the north. A numerous tribe, <reference osisRef="Num.26.25">Num. xxvi. 25</reference>. Tola, one of the judges, was of this tribe, <reference osisRef="Judg.10.1">Judg. x. 1</reference>. So was Baasha, one of the kings of Israel, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.15.27">1 Kings xv. 27</reference>. The most considerable places in this tribe were, 1. Jezreel, in which was Ahab's palace, and near it Naboth's vineyard. 2. Shunem, where lived that good Shunamite that entertained Elisha. 3. The river Kishon, on the banks of which, in this tribe, Sisera was beaten by Deborah and Barak. 4. The mountains of Gilboa, on which Saul and Jonathan were slain, which were not far from Endor, where Saul consulted the witch. 5. The valley of Megiddo, where Josiah was slain near Hadad-rimmon, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.23.29">2 Kings xxiii. 29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.11">Zech. xii. 11</reference>.
entries.b811efc2f63154fc8d8a3ceacbc60744d4e63ad6: <div eID="gen4469" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Lot of Asher. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4470" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">24</hi> And the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families. <hi type="super">25</hi> And their border was Helkath, and Hali, and Beten, and Achshaph, <hi type="super">26</hi> And Alammelech, and Amad, and Misheal; and reacheth to Carmel westward, and to Shihor-libnath; <hi type="super">27</hi> And turneth toward the sunrising to Beth-dagon, and reacheth to Zebulun, and to the valley of Jiphthah-el toward the north side of Beth-emek, and Neiel, and goeth out to Cabul on the left hand, <hi type="super">28</hi> And Hebron, and Rehob, and Hammon, and Kanah, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto great Zidon; <hi type="super">29</hi> And <hi type="italic">then</hi> the coast turneth to Ramah, and to the strong city Tyre; and the coast turneth to Hosah; and the outgoings thereof are at the sea from the coast to Achzib: <hi type="super">30</hi> Ummah also, and Aphek, and Rehob: twenty and two cities with their villages. <hi type="super">31</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families, these cities with their villages. <div eID="gen4470" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4471" type="x-p"/> The lot of Asher lay upon the coast of the great sea. We read not of any famous person of this tribe but Anna the prophetess, who was a constant resident in the temple at the time of our Saviour's birth, <reference osisRef="Luke.2.36">Luke ii. 36</reference>. Nor were there many famous places in this tribe. Aphek (mentioned <reference osisRef="Josh.19.30">v. 30</reference>) was the place near which Benhadad was beaten by Ahad, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.20.30">1 Kings xx. 30</reference>. But close adjoining to this tribe were the celebrated sea-port towns of Tyre and Sidon, which we read so much of. Tyre is called here <hi type="italic">that strong city</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.29">v. 29</reference>), but Bishop Patrick thinks it was not the same Tyre that we read of afterwards, for that was built on an island; this old strong city was on the continent. And it is conjectured by some that into these two strong-holds, Sidon and Tzor, or Tyre, many of the people of Canaan fled and took shelter when Joshua invaded them.
entries.81a563f9883922a30edb6aa3c69ba15e691821ac: <div eID="gen4471" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Lot of Naphtali. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4472" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">32</hi> The sixth lot came out to the children of Naphtali, <hi type="italic">even</hi> for the children of Naphtali according to their families. <hi type="super">33</hi> And their coast was from Heleph, from Allon to Zaanannim, and Adami, Nekeb, and Jabneel, unto Lakum; and the outgoings thereof were at Jordan: <hi type="super">34</hi> And <hi type="italic">then</hi> the coast turneth westward to Aznoth-tabor, and goeth out from thence to Hukkok, and reacheth to Zebulun on the south side, and reacheth to Asher on the west side, and to Judah upon Jordan toward the sunrising. <hi type="super">35</hi> And the fenced cities <hi type="italic">are</hi> Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth, <hi type="super">36</hi> And Adamah, and Ramah, and Hazor, <hi type="super">37</hi> And Kedesh, and Edrei, and En-hazor, <hi type="super">38</hi> And Iron, and Migdal-el, Horem, and Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh; nineteen cities with their villages. <hi type="super">39</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities and their villages. <div eID="gen4472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4473" type="x-p"/> Naphtali lay furthest north of all the tribes, bordering on Mount Libanus. The city of Leshem, or Liash, lay on the utmost edge of it to the north, and therefore when the Danites had made themselves masters of it, and called it <hi type="italic">Dan,</hi> the length of Canaan from north to south was reckoned from Dan to Beersheba. It had Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah upon Jordan, probably a city of that name, and so distinguished from the tribe of Judah on the east. It was in the lot of this tribe, near the waters of Merom, that Joshua fought and routed Jabin, <reference osisRef="Josh.11.1-Josh.11.14">ch. xi. 1</reference>. &c. In this tribe stood Capernaum and Bethsaida, on the north end of the sea of Tiberias, in which Christ did so many mighty works; and the mountain (as is supposed) on which Christ preached, <reference osisRef="Matt.5.1">Matt. v. 1</reference>.
entries.c8b6ef08dd832d140667f580738046c71dfd289b: <div eID="gen4473" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Lot of Dan. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4474" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">40</hi> <hi type="italic">And</hi> the seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families. <hi type="super">41</hi> And the coast of their inheritance was Zorah, and Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh, <hi type="super">42</hi> And Shaalabbin, and Ajalon, and Jethlah, <hi type="super">43</hi> And Elon, and Thimnathah, and Ekron, <hi type="super">44</hi> And Eltekeh, and Gibbethon, and Baalath, <hi type="super">45</hi> And Jehud, and Bene-berak, and Gath-rimmon, <hi type="super">46</hi> And Me-jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border before Japho. <hi type="super">47</hi> And the coast of the children of Dan went out <hi type="italic">too little</hi> for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father. <hi type="super">48</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, these cities with their villages. <div eID="gen4474" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4475" type="x-p"/> Dan, though commander of one of the four squadrons of the camp of Israel, in the wilderness, that which brought up the rear, yet was last provided for in Canaan, and his lot fell in the southern part of Canaan, between Judah on the east and the land of the Philistines on the west, Ephraim on the north and Simeon on the south. Providence ordered this numerous and powerful tribe into a post of danger, as best able to deal with those vexatious neighbours the Philistines, and so it was found in Samson. Here is an account, 1. Of what fell to this tribe by lot, Zorah, and Eshtaol, and the camp of Dan thereabouts, of which we read in the story of Samson. And near there was the valley of Eshcol, whence the spies brought the famous bunch of grapes. Japho, or Joppa was in this lot. 2. Of what they got by their own industry and valour, which is mentioned here (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.47">v. 47</reference>), but related at large, <reference osisRef="Judg.18.7-Judg.18.31">Judg. xviii. 7</reference>, &c.
entries.dd1bc0fb9984341a3e478a43319a3928bf55b373: <div eID="gen4475" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Inheritance of Joshua. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen4476" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">49</hi> When they had made an end of dividing the land for inheritance by their coasts, the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun among them: <hi type="super">50</hi> According to the word of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> they gave him the city which he asked, <hi type="italic">even</hi> Timnath-serah in mount Ephraim: and he built the city, and dwelt therein. <hi type="super">51</hi> These <hi type="italic">are</hi> the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel, divided for an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country. <div eID="gen4476" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4477" type="x-p"/> Before this account of the dividing of the land is solemnly closed up, in the <reference osisRef="Josh.19.51">last verse</reference>, which intimates that the thing was done to the satisfaction of all, here is an account of the particular inheritance assigned to <reference osisRef="Josh.1">Joshua. 1</reference>. He was last served, though the eldest and greatest man of all Israel, and who, having commanded in the conquest of Canaan, might have demanded the first settlement in it for himself and his family. But he would make it to appear that in all he did he sought the good of his country, and not any private interest of his own. He was content to be unfixed till he saw them all settled; and herein is a great example to all in public places to prefer the common welfare before their particular satisfaction. Let the public be first served. 2. He had his lot <hi type="italic">according to the word of the Lord.</hi> It is probable that, when God by Moses told Caleb what inheritance he should have (<reference osisRef="Josh.14.9">ch. xiv. 9</reference>), he gave the like promise to Joshua, which he had an eye to in making his election: this made his portion doubly pleasant, that he had it, not as the rest by common providence, but by special promise. 3. He chose it in Mount Ephraim, which belonged to his own tribe, with which he thereby put himself in common, when he might by prerogative have chosen his inheritance in some other tribe, as suppose that of Judah, and thereby have distinguished himself from them. Let no man's preferment or honour make him ashamed of his family or country, or estrange him from it. The tabernacle was set up in the lot of Ephraim, and Joshua would forecast not to be far from that. 4. The <hi type="italic">children of Israel</hi> are said to <hi type="italic">give it to him</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.49">v. 49</reference>), which bespeaks his humility, that he would not take it to himself without the people's consent and approbation, as if he would thereby own himself, though <hi type="italic">major singulis—greater than any one,</hi> yet <hi type="italic">minor universis—less than the whole assemblage,</hi> and would hold even the estate of his family, under God, by the grant of the people. 5. It was a city that must be built before it was fit to be dwelt in. While others dwelt in houses which they built not, Joshua must erect for himself (that he might be a pattern of industry and contentment with mean things) such buildings as he could hastily run up, without curiosity or magnificence. Our Lord Jesus thus came and dwelt among us, not in pomp but poverty, providing rest for us, yet himself not having where to lay his head. <hi type="italic">Even Christ pleased not himself.</hi>  <chapter eID="Josh.19"/> <div eID="gen4477" type="x-p"/>

entries.69158cedb420cefb29740618622011b4a5ae0731: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2151"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 19</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.1-Josh.19.9">Jos 19:1-9</reference>. The Lot of Simeon.</title> <div sID="gen2894" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2151"/><hi type="bold">1. the second lot came forth to Simeon--</hi>The next lot that was drawn at Shiloh, gave the tribe of Simeon his inheritance within the territory, which had been assigned to that of Judah. The knowledge of Canaan possessed by the Israelites, when the division of the land commenced, was but very general, being derived from the rapid sweep they had made over it during the course of conquest; and it was on the ground of that rough survey alone that the distribution proceeded, by which Judah received an inheritance. Time showed that this territory was too large (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.9">Jos 19:9</reference>), either for their numbers, however great, to occupy and their arms to defend, or too large in proportion to the allotments of the other tribes. Justice therefore required (what kind and brotherly feeling readily dictated) a modification of their possession; and a part of it was appropriated to Simeon. By thus establishing it within the original domain of another tribe, the prophecy of Jacob in regard to Simeon was fulfilled (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Ge 49:7</reference>); for from its boundaries being not traced, there is reason to conclude that its people were divided and dispersed among those of Judah; and though one group of its cities named (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.2-Josh.19.6">Jos 19:2-6</reference>), gives the idea of a compact district, as it is usually represented by map makers, the other group (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.7">Jos 19:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.8">8</reference>) were situated, two in the south, and two elsewhere, with tracts of the country around them. <div eID="gen2894" type="x-p"/>
entries.bfd779ba8cfb08cb306f040f0a06cb13ed0bf04a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2152"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.10-Josh.19.16">Jos 19:10-16</reference>. Of Zebulun.</title> <div sID="gen2895" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2152"/><hi type="bold">10-14. the third lot came up for the children of Zebulun--</hi>The boundaries of the possession assigned to them extended from the Lake of Chinnereth (Sea of Galilee) on the east, to the Mediterranean on the west. Although they do not seem at first to have touched on the western shore--a part of Manasseh running north into Asher (<reference osisRef="Josh.17.10">Jos 17:10</reference>)--they afterwards did, according to the prediction of Moses (<reference osisRef="Deut.33.19">De 33:19</reference>). The extent from north to south cannot be very exactly traced; the sites of many of the places through which the boundary line is drawn being unknown. Some of the cities were of note. <div eID="gen2895" type="x-p"/>
entries.53c4cd21682c712239ff11aa2977f53d48a5edd3: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2153"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.17-Josh.19.23">Jos 19:17-23</reference>. Of Issachar.</title> <div sID="gen2896" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2153"/><hi type="bold">17-20. the fourth lot came out to Issachar--</hi>Instead of describing the boundaries of this tribe, the inspired historian gives a list of its principal cities. These cities are all in the eastern part of the plain of Esdraelon. <div eID="gen2896" type="x-p"/>
entries.46ee48f878e7bf9e945c7615e36969bdac39be77: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2154"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.24-Josh.19.31">Jos 19:24-31</reference>. Of Asher.</title> <div sID="gen2897" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2154"/><hi type="bold">24-31. the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher--</hi>The western boundary is traced from north to south through the cities mentioned; the site of them, however, is unknown. <div eID="gen2897" type="x-p"/>
entries.58f6d5ad1b49f723940818d7db40ee99c454db8a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2157"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.32-Josh.19.39">Jos 19:32-39</reference>. Of Naphtali.</title> <div sID="gen2901" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2157"/><hi type="bold">32-39. the sixth lot came out to the children of Naphtali--</hi>Although the cities mentioned have not been discovered, it is evident, from Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh, that is, on the northwest of Lake Merom (<reference osisRef="Judg.4.11">Jud 4:11</reference>), that the boundary described (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.34">Jos 19:34</reference>) ran from the southwest towards the northeast, up to the sources of the Jordan. <div eID="gen2901" type="x-p"/>
entries.f4c17273fafdba50698ccc1d45775b891aa65a70: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2159"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.40-Josh.19.48">Jos 19:40-48</reference>. Of Dan.</title> <div sID="gen2904" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2159"/><hi type="bold">40-46. the seventh lot came out for the tribe ... Dan--</hi>It lay on the west of Benjamin and consisted of portions surrendered by Judah and Ephraim. Its boundaries are not stated, as they were easily distinguishable from the relative position of Dan to the three adjoining tribes. <div eID="gen2904" type="x-p"/>
entries.522d98902bebb03a8ed01a9b101dd8701305ff09: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2160"/><div sID="gen2905" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2160"/><hi type="bold">47. the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem--</hi>The Danites, finding their inheritance too small, decided to enlarge its boundaries by the sword; and, having conquered Leshem (Laish), they planted a colony there, calling the new settlement by the name of Dan (see on <reference osisRef="Judg.18.7">Jud 18:7</reference>). <div eID="gen2905" type="x-p"/>
entries.6a5fe10cc6a850f716db41e388d9733a601d9226: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2161"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.49-Josh.19.51">Jos 19:49-51</reference>. The Children of Israel Give an Inheritance to Joshua.</title> <div sID="gen2906" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2161"/><hi type="bold">50. According to the word of the Lord they gave him the city which he asked--</hi>It was most proper that the great leader should receive an inheritance suited to his dignity, and as a reward for his public services. But the gift was not left to the spontaneous feelings of a grateful people. It was conferred "according to the word of the Lord"--probably an unrecorded promise, similar to what had been made to Caleb (<reference osisRef="Josh.14.9">Jos 14:9</reference>).<div eID="gen2906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2907" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Timnath-serah--</hi>or Heres, on Mount Gaash (<reference osisRef="Judg.2.9">Jud 2:9</reference>). Joshua founded it, and was afterwards buried there (<reference osisRef="Josh.24.30">Jos 24:30</reference>). <div eID="gen2907" type="x-p"/>
entries.dd8f000493e23563b335e5a6cb0e672c51f53224: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2162"/><div sID="gen2908" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2162"/><hi type="bold">51. These are the inheritances--</hi>This verse is the formal close of the section which narrates the history of the land distribution; and to stamp it with due importance, the names of the commissioners are repeated, as well as the spot where so memorable a transaction took place. <chapter eID="Josh.19"/>

entries.156cf69fce716fe3cc4693f45f5ca389fb465c79: <div eID="gen8097" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen8098" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen8099" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen8099" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen8098" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen8100" type="x-p"/> The lot of Simeon, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.1-Jos.19.9">Jos 19:1-9</reference>. Of Zebulun, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.10-Jos.19.16">Jos 19:10-16</reference>. Of Issachar, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.17-Jos.19.23">Jos 19:17-23</reference>. Of Asher, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.24-Jos.19.31">Jos 19:24-31</reference>. Of Naphtali, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.32-Jos.19.39">Jos 19:32-39</reference>. Of Dan, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.40-Jos.19.48">Jos 19:40-48</reference>. Joshua's portion, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.49">Jos 19:49</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.50">Jos 19:50</reference>. The conclusion of the division of the land, <reference osisRef="Jos.19.51">Jos 19:51</reference>. <div eID="gen8100" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8101" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen8101" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8102" type="x-p"/> The second lot came forth to Simeon - In this appointment the providence of God may be especially remarked. For the iniquitous conduct of Simeon and Levi, in the massacre of the innocent Shechemites, <reference osisRef="Gen.34.25-Gen.34.31">Gen 34:25-31</reference>, Jacob, in the spirit of prophecy, foretold that they should be divided in Jacob, and scattered in Israel, <reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Gen 49:7</reference>. And this was most literally fulfilled in the manner in which God disposed of both these tribes afterwards. Levi was scattered through all Palestine, not having received any inheritance, only cities to dwell in, in different parts of the land; and Simeon was dispersed in Judah, with what could scarcely be said to be their own, or a peculiar lot. See the note on <reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Gen 49:7</reference>.
entries.b2335f7c9fff9f0fc765c23ab5b8cf2d4ae93d6d: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen8102" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8103" type="x-p"/> Beer-sheba - The well of the oath. See the note on <reference osisRef="Gen.21.31">Gen 21:31</reference>.
entries.36e967e5e0543b773c796af9f719eb56dc632d47: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen8103" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8104" type="x-p"/> Hazar-shual - For this and several of the following places, see the notes on <reference osisRef="Jos.15.32">Jos 15:32</reference>.
entries.1fe96c2f5eaf3cae9c37c2509e9877e19fd84373: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen8104" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8105" type="x-p"/> Beth-marcaboth - The house or city of chariots. Probably a place where their war-chariots and cavalry were laid up.
entries.776f8038ed6faaa8bc997b160a80b164f110d0b7: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen8105" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8106" type="x-p"/> Beth-lebaoth - The house or city of lionesses. Probably so called from the numbers of those animals which bred there.
entries.7bdc4022d1dea721f2360d2266448936291b522f: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen8106" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8107" type="x-p"/> Baalath-beer - The well of the mistresses. Probably so called from some superstitious or impure worship set up there.
entries.d4705fd5da713fa4447458fa0e33f1fc9442a90e: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen8107" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8108" type="x-p"/> Gittah-hepher - The same as Gath-hepher, the birth-place of the prophet Jonah.
entries.1e5c30501ffcc012249684fe57d65556d33af941: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen8108" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8109" type="x-p"/> Shimron - See on <reference osisRef="Jos.12.20">Jos 12:20</reference> (note). <div eID="gen8109" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8110" type="x-p"/> Beth-lehem - The house of bread; a different place from that in which our Lord was born.
entries.54d0e60b3b14209538a330a7f78883d4d2f45550: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen8110" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8111" type="x-p"/> The fourth lot came out to Issachar - It is remarkable, that though Issachar was the eldest brother, yet the lot of Zebulun was drawn before his lot; and this is the order in which Jacob himself mentions them, <reference osisRef="Gen.49.13">Gen 49:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.49.14">Gen 49:14</reference>, though no reason appears, either here or in the place above, why this preference should be given to the younger; but that the apparently fortuitous lot should have distinguished them just as the prophetic Jacob did, is peculiarly remarkable. Known unto God are all his works from the beginning: he has reasons for his conduct, which in many cases are too great for any of his creatures to comprehend, but he works all things after the counsel of his own will, which is ever right and good; and in this case his influence may be as easily seen in the decision by the lot, as on the mind of the patriarch Jacob, when he predicted what should befall his children in the latter days, and his providence continued to ripen, and bring forward what his judgment had deemed right to be done.
entries.eacddb9c4cae1a28354aaacba413156a2ac1fc34: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen8111" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8112" type="x-p"/> Jezreel - This city, according to Calmet, was situated in an open country, having the town of Legion on the west, Bethshan on the east, on the south the mountains of Gilboa, and on the north those of Hermon. <div eID="gen8112" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8113" type="x-p"/> Shunem - This city was rendered famous by being the occasional abode of the prophet Elisha, and the place where he restored the son of a pious woman to life. <reference osisRef="2Kgs.4.8">2Kgs 4:8</reference>. It was the place where the Philistines were encamped on that ruinous day in which the Israelites were totally routed at Gilboa, and Saul and his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, killed. <reference osisRef="1Sam.28.4">1Sam 28:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.31.1">1Sam 31:1</reference>, etc.
entries.cf5f63e1d1e47ab92fe2ab9f81d73c3e29753a05: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen8113" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8114" type="x-p"/> Beth-shemesh - The house or temple of the sun; there were several cities or towns of this name in Palestine; an ample proof that the worship of this celestial luminary had generally prevailed in that idolatrous country.
entries.b84a589f5019b16c2537fd4944a61b94e5f155a7: <hi type="bold">Verse 26</hi> <div eID="gen8114" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8115" type="x-p"/> Carmel - The vineyard of God; a place greatly celebrated in Scripture, and especially for the miracles of Elijah; see 1 Kings 18:19-40. The mountain of Carmel was so very fruitful as to pass into a proverb. There was another Carmel in the tribe of Judah, (see <reference osisRef="Jos.15.55">Jos 15:55</reference>), but this, in the tribe of Asher, was situated about one hundred and twenty furlongs south from Ptolemais, on the edge of the Mediterranean Sea. Calmet observes that there was, in the time of Vespasian, a temple on this mountain, dedicated to a god of the same name. There was a convent, and a religious order known by the name of Carmelites, established on this mountain in honor of Elijah: the time of the foundation of this order is greatly disputed. Some pretend that it was established by Elijah himself; while others, with more probability, fix it in a.d. 1180 or 1181, under the pontificate of Pope Alexander III.
entries.e104c8b80abfe3e6138141cc3996ae9036f2c297: <hi type="bold">Verse 27</hi> <div eID="gen8115" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8116" type="x-p"/> Cabul on the left hand - That is, to the north of Cabul, for so the left hand, when referring to place, is understood among the Hebrews. We must not confound this town or Cabul with the twenty cities given by Solomon to Hiram, with which he was displeased, and which in contempt he called the land of Cabul, the dirty or paltry land, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.9.11-1Kgs.9.13">1Kgs 9:11-13</reference> : there was evidently a town of this name, widely different from the land so called, long before the time of Solomon, and therefore this cannot be adduced as an argument that the book of Joshua was written after the days of David. The town in question is supposed to be the same which Josephus in his Life calls Χωβουλω Choboulo, and which he says was situated by the sea-side, and nigh to Ptolemais. De Bell. Jud., lib. iii., c. 4.
entries.8cbeeaa241197a7ade3f84bbb665f28eb1c80555: <hi type="bold">Verse 28</hi> <div eID="gen8116" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8117" type="x-p"/> Unto great Zidon - The city of Sidon and the Sidonians are celebrated from the remotest antiquity. They are frequently mentioned by Homer. See the note on <reference osisRef="Jos.11.8">Jos 11:8</reference>.
entries.da4e6a0ceb75c79cf97b2df1a1f1947ea5219bbe: <hi type="bold">Verse 29</hi> <div eID="gen8117" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8118" type="x-p"/> The strong city Tyre - I suspect this to be an improper translation. Perhaps the words of the original should be retained: And the coast turneth to Ramah and to the city, מבצר צר mibtsar tsor. Our translators have here left the Hebrew, and followed the Septuagint and Vulgate, a fault of which they are sometimes guilty. The former render the place ἑως πολεως οχυρωματος των Τυριων, unto the fortified city of the Tyrians. The Vulgate is nearly the same: ad civitatem munitissimam Tyrum, to the well-fortified city Tyre; but this must be incorrect for the famous city of Tyre was not known till about A.M. 2760, about two hundred years after the days of Joshua. Homer, who frequently mentions Sidon and the Sidonians, never mentions Tyre; a proof that this afterwards very eminent city was not then known. Homer is allowed by some to have flourished in the time of Joshua, though others make him contemporary with the Israelitish judges. The word צר Tsor or Tsar, which we translate or change into Tyre, signifies a rock or strong place; and as there were many rocks in the land of Judea, that with a little art were formed into strong places of defense, hence several places might have the name of Tsar or Tyre. The ancient and celebrated Tyre, so much spoken of both in sacred and profane history, was a rock or small island in the sea, about six or seven hundred paces from the main land. In order to reduce this city, Alexander the Great was obliged to fill up the channel between it and the main land, and after all took it with much difficulty. It is generally supposed that a town on the main land, opposite to this fortified rock, went by the same name; one being called old Tyre, the other, new Tyre: it was out of the ruins of the old Tyre, or that which was situated on the main land, that Alexander is said to have filled up the channel between it and the new city. Of this city Isaiah, Isaiah 23:1-18, and Ezekiel, Ezekiel 27:1-28:26, have given a very grand description, and also predicted its irreparable ruin which prophecies have been most literally fulfilled. See more on the above places. <div eID="gen8118" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8119" type="x-p"/> Achzib - Called afterwards Ecdippe, and now called Zib; it is about nine miles' distance from Ptolemais, towards Tyre.
entries.7a6b4cf810b5a888375c2f18b5a89c1410d2dbf9: <hi type="bold">Verse 30</hi> <div eID="gen8119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8120" type="x-p"/> Twenty and two cities - There are nearly thirty cities in the above enumeration instead of twenty-two, but probably several are mentioned that were but frontier towns, and that did not belong to this tribe, their border only passing by such cities; and on this account, though they are named, yet they do not enter into the enumeration in this place. Perhaps some of the villages are named as well as the cities.
entries.edb80bc24f24ce8a6d5b9852bdd4754f006cffd9: <hi type="bold">Verse 34</hi> <div eID="gen8120" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8121" type="x-p"/> And to Judah upon Jordan - It is certain that the tribe of Naphtali did not border on the east upon Judah, for there were several tribes betwixt them. Some think that as these two tribes were bounded by Jordan on the east, they might be considered as in some sort conjoined, because of the easy passage to each other by means of the river; but this might be said of several other tribes as well as of these. There is considerable difficulty in the text as it now stands; but if, with the Septuagint, we omit Judah, the difficulty vanishes, and the passage is plain: but this omission is supported by no MS. hitherto discovered. It is however very probable that some change has taken place in the words of the text, וביהודה הירדן ubihudah haiyarden, "and by Judah upon Jordan." Houbigant, who terms them verba sine re ac sententia, "words without sense or meaning," proposes, instead of them, to read ובגדות הירדן ubigdoth haiyarden, "and by the banks of Jordan;" a word which is used <reference osisRef="Jos.3.15">Jos 3:15</reference>, and which here makes a very good sense.
entries.d0c842477a8845cbd36556ef70e4075871983876: <hi type="bold">Verse 35</hi> <div eID="gen8121" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8122" type="x-p"/> Chinnereth - See the note on <reference osisRef="Jos.11.2">Jos 11:2</reference>.
entries.1c988c29b29b94680872701cea8b855fc5a2eb0b: <hi type="bold">Verse 36</hi> <div eID="gen8122" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8123" type="x-p"/> Hazor - See the note on <reference osisRef="Jos.11.1">Jos 11:1</reference>.
entries.ff0b03f90cbf6316e31f6a964ffad8bafdc556b4: <hi type="bold">Verse 38</hi> <div eID="gen8123" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8124" type="x-p"/> Nineteen cities - But if these cities be separately enumerated they amount to twenty-three; this is probably occasioned by reckoning frontier cities belonging to other tribes, which are only mentioned here as the boundaries of the tribe. See on <reference osisRef="Jos.19.30">Jos 19:30</reference> (note).
entries.34049cfa5fe644c59ac93edac60355f8f575237e: <hi type="bold">Verse 41</hi> <div eID="gen8124" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8125" type="x-p"/> Zorah, and Eshtaol - See the note on <reference osisRef="Jos.15.33">Jos 15:33</reference>. <div eID="gen8125" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8126" type="x-p"/> Ir-shemesh - The city of sun; another proof of the idolatry of the Canaanites. Some think this was the same as Beth-shemesh.
entries.eb396c6447f782b6f70aacbba4fb57b4a625124c: <hi type="bold">Verse 42</hi> <div eID="gen8126" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8127" type="x-p"/> Shaalabbin - The foxes. Of this city the Amorites kept constant possession. See <reference osisRef="Jdg.1.35">Jdg 1:35</reference>. <div eID="gen8127" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8128" type="x-p"/> Ajalon - There was a place of this name about two miles from Nicopolis or Emmaus, on the road to Jerusalem. - Calmet.
entries.fb6a09d76f926d385beb1c0a2fbd5fab1f28b74b: <hi type="bold">Verse 43</hi> <div eID="gen8128" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8129" type="x-p"/> Thimnathah - Probably the same as Timnah. See on <reference osisRef="Jos.15.57">Jos 15:57</reference> (note). <div eID="gen8129" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8130" type="x-p"/> Ekron - A well-known city of the Philistines and the metropolis of one of their five dynasties.
entries.b1fd6efe2dc7b4afb790081b95fc849b33f1d202: <hi type="bold">Verse 45</hi> <div eID="gen8130" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8131" type="x-p"/> Jehud, and Bene-berak - Or Jehud of the children of Berak.
entries.7186661c1beb8e8a4d8cee1833d9a25cd86bc8a6: <hi type="bold">Verse 46</hi> <div eID="gen8131" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8132" type="x-p"/> Japho - The place since called Joppa, lying on the Mediterranean, and the chief sea-port, in the possession of the twelve tribes.
entries.83455dff44619310575a42c7493cd8e1032409f1: <hi type="bold">Verse 47</hi> <div eID="gen8132" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8133" type="x-p"/> Went out too little for them - This is certainly the meaning of the passage; but our translators have been obliged to add the words too little to make this sense apparent. Houbigant contends that an ancient copyist, meeting frequently with the words ויצאהגבול vaiyetse haggebul, in the preceding history, became so familiarized to them that he wrote them here instead of ויאץ הגבול vaiyaats haggebul, and the border of the children of Dan was Strait for them. It was on this account that they were obliged to go and fight against Leshem, and take and possess it, their former inheritance being too strait for their increasing population. <div eID="gen8133" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8134" type="x-p"/> And called Leshem, Dan - This city was situated near the origin of Jordan, at the utmost northern extremity of the promised land, as Beer-sheba was at that of the south; and as after its capture by the Danites it was called Dan, hence arose the expression from Dan even to Beer-sheba, which always signified the whole extent of the promised land. Some suppose that Leshem was the same with Caesarea Philippi, but others with reason reject this opinion. It must be granted that the whole account given in this verse refers indisputably to a fact which did not take place till after the death of Joshua. It is another of the marginal or explicative notes which were added by some later hand. The whole account of this expedition of the Danites against Leshem is circumstantially given in the book of Judges, chapter 18, and to that chapter the reader is referred.
entries.8e578bf623e209fadb7ceab9054068d99444b7af: <hi type="bold">Verse 50</hi> <div eID="gen8134" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8135" type="x-p"/> Timnath-serah - Called Timnath-heres in <reference osisRef="Jdg.2.9">Jdg 2:9</reference>, where we find that the mountain on which it was built was called Gaash. It is generally allowed to have been a barren spot in a barren country.
entries.7e5f7c8f8155dbf186f14a5c3f32057e6b4ec5e6: <hi type="bold">Verse 51</hi> <div eID="gen8135" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8136" type="x-p"/> At the door of the tabernacle - All the inheritances were determined by lot, and this was cast before the Lord - every thing was done in his immediate presence, as under his eye; hence there was no murmuring, each having received his inheritance as from the hand of God himself, though some of them thought they must have additional territory, because of the great increase of their families.  <chapter eID="Josh.19"/> <div eID="gen8136" type="x-p"/>

entries.6b76fe9634ef0c29ca0576a92d3fbd8069a1004c: <div eID="gen2929" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">INHERITANCE OF THE TRIBES OF SIMEON, ZEBULUN, ISSACHAB, ASHER, NAPHTALI, AND DAN. CHAP. XIX.</title> <div sID="gen2930" type="x-p"/> The Inheritance of Simeon fell within the inheritance of the children of Judah, because the land allotted to them at Gilgal was larger than they required (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.9">Jos 19:9</reference>). Thus the curse pronounced upon Simeon by Jacob of dispersion in Israel (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Gen 49:7</reference>) was fulfilled upon this tribe in a very peculiar manner, and in a different manner from that pronounced upon Levi. The towns allotted to the tribe of Simeon are divided into two groups, the first (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.2-Josh.19.6">Jos 19:2-6</reference>) consisting of thirteen or fourteen towns, all situated in the Negeb (or south country); the second (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.7">Jos 19:7</reference>) of four towns, two of which were in the <hi type="italic">Negeb</hi> and two in the <hi type="italic">shephelah</hi>. All these eighteen towns have already been enumerated among the towns of Judah (<reference osisRef="Josh.15.26-Josh.15.32">Jos 15:26-32</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.15.42">Jos 15:42</reference>), and are mentioned again in <reference osisRef="1Chr.4.28-1Chr.4.32">1Ch 4:28-32</reference>, in just the same order, and with only slight differences in the spelling of some of the names. If the classification of the names in two groups might seem to indicate that Simeon received a connected portion of land in Judah, this idea is overthrown at once by the circumstance that two of the four towns in the second group were in the south land and two in the lowland, and, judging from <reference osisRef="Josh.15.32">Jos 15:32</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.15.42">Jos 15:42</reference>, at a great distance from one another. At the same time, we cannot decide this point with any certainty, as the situation of several of the towns is still unknown.
entries.eddf6b22dc60dfed0a80d9ee85e071a40b851e90: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.2-Josh.19.6">Jos 19:2-6</reference> <hi type="italic">Beersheba:</hi> see at Jos 15:28. <hi type="italic">Sheba</hi> is wanting in the Chronicles, but has no doubt been omitted through a copyist’s error, as <hi type="italic">Shema</hi> answers to it in <reference osisRef="Josh.15.26">Jos 15:26</reference>, where it stands before <hi type="italic">Moladah</hi> just as Sheba does here. - On the names in <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.3-Josh.19.6">Jos 19:3-6</reference></hi>, see the exposition of <reference osisRef="Josh.15.28">Jos 15:28</reference>-32. - The sum total given in <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Josh.19.6">Jos 19:6</reference></hi>, viz., thirteen towns, does not tally, as there are fourteen names. On these differences, see the remarks on Jos 15:32.
entries.09684f8eb4e3148f5584bea98f7366802972a485: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.7">Jos 19:7</reference> <hi type="italic">Ain</hi> and <hi type="italic">Rimmon</hi> were in the south land (<reference osisRef="Josh.15.32">Jos 15:32</reference>), <hi type="italic">Ether</hi> and <hi type="italic">Ashan</hi> in the lowlands (<reference osisRef="Josh.15.42">Jos 15:42</reference>).
entries.84d6af8d9ad20b3e76040b22a6bec52c0605b6e7: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.8-Josh.19.9">Jos 19:8-9</reference> <div eID="gen2930" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2931" type="x-p"/> In addition to the towns mentioned, the Simeonites received all the villages round about the towns to <hi type="italic">Baalath-beer</hi>, the <hi type="italic">Ramah</hi> of <hi type="italic">the south</hi>. This place, up to which the territory of the Simeonites extended, though without its being actually assigned to the Simeonites, is simply called Baal in <reference osisRef="1Chr.4.33">1Ch 4:33</reference>, and is probably the same as <hi type="italic">Bealoth</hi> in <reference osisRef="Josh.15.24">Jos 15:24</reference>, though its situation has not yet been determined (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.15.24">Jos 15:24</reference>). It cannot be identified, however, with <hi type="italic">Ramet el Khulil</hi>, an hour to the north of Hebron, which <hi type="italic">Roediger</hi> supposes to be the Ramah of the south, since the territory of Simeon, which was situated in the Negeb, and had only two towns in the <hi type="italic">shephelah</hi>, cannot possibly have extended into the mountains to a point on the north of Hebron. So far as the situation is concerned, <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi> would be more likely to be correct, when he identifies <hi type="italic">Rama of the south</hi> with Tell <hi type="italic">Lekiyeh</hi> on the north of Beersheba, if this conjecture only rested upon a better foundation than the untenable assumption, that Baalath-beer is the same as the Baalath of Dan in Jos 19:44. <div eID="gen2931" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2932" type="x-p"/> The Inheritance of Zebulun fell above the plain of Jezreel, between this plain and the mountains of Naphtali, so that it was bounded by Asher on the west and north-west (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.27">Jos 19:27</reference>), by Naphtali on the north and north-east (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.34">Jos 19:34</reference>), and by Issachar on the south-east and south, and touched neither the Mediterranean Sea nor the Jordan. It embraced a very fertile country, however, with the fine broad plain of <hi type="italic">el Buttauf</hi>, the μέγα πεδίον above Nazareth called <hi type="italic">Asochis</hi> in <hi type="italic">Joseph</hi>.<hi type="italic">vita</hi>, §41, 45 (see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 189, Bibl. Res. pp. 105ff.; <hi type="italic">Ritter</hi>, Erdk. xvi. pp. 742, 758-9).
entries.4c0f8896a6f1ca6e74d9eea7ba9c2f304d1c2c55: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.10">Jos 19:10</reference> <div eID="gen2932" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2933" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">And the boundary</hi> (the territory) <hi type="italic">of their inheritance was</hi> (went) <hi type="italic">to Sarid</hi>.” This is no doubt the centre of the southern boundary, from which it is traced in a westerly direction in <reference osisRef="Josh.19.11">Jos 19:11</reference>, and in an easterly direction in <reference osisRef="Josh.19.12">Jos 19:12</reference>, in the same manner as in Jos 16:6. Unfortunately, Sarid cannot be determined with certainty. <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi>'s opinion, is, that the name, which signifies “hole” or “incision,” after the analogy of שׂרד, <hi type="italic">perforavit</hi>, and שׂרט, <hi type="italic">incidit</hi>, does not refer to a town, but to some other locality, probably the southern opening of the deep and narrow wady which comes down from the basin of Nazareth, and is about an hour to the south-east of Nazareth, between two steep mountains (<hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. pp. 151-2; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 183). This locality appears suitable enough. But it is also possible that <hi type="italic">Sarid</hi> may be found in one of the two heaps of ruins on the south side of the <hi type="italic">Mons praecipitii</hi> upon <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi>'s map (so called from <reference osisRef="Luke.4.29">Luk 4:29</reference>).
entries.bb2ef3f2a3b040faced578752eac4870dd8e93df: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.11">Jos 19:11</reference> <div eID="gen2933" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2934" type="x-p"/> From this point “<hi type="italic">the border went up westwards, namely to Mar'ala, and touched Dabbasheth, and still farther to the brook of Jokneam</hi>.” If <hi type="italic">Jokneam</hi> of Carmel has been preserved in the Tell <hi type="italic">Kaimûn</hi> (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.12.22">Jos 12:22</reference>), the brook before Jokneam is probably the Wady <hi type="italic">el Milh</hi>, on the eastern side of which, near the point where it opens into the plain, stands <hi type="italic">Kaimûn</hi>, and through which the road runs from Acca to Ramleh, as this wady separates Carmel from the small round hills which run to the south-east (see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. p. 114, and <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi>, i. p. 249). Here the boundaries of Zebulun and Asher met (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.27">Jos 19:27</reference>). <hi type="italic">Mar'ala</hi> and <hi type="italic">Dabbasheth</hi> are to be sought for between Kaimûn and Sarid. The <hi type="italic">Cod. Vat.</hi> has Μαγελδά instead of Μαριλά. Now, however, little importance we can attach to the readings of the lxx on account of the senseless way in which its renderings are made-as, for example, in this very passage, where ועלה עד־שׂריד׃ is rendered Ἐσεδεκγώλα, - the name <hi type="italic">Magelda</hi> might suggest a Hebrew reading <hi type="italic">Magedlah</hi> or <hi type="italic">Mageldah</hi>, and thus lead one to connect the place with the village of <hi type="italic">Mejeidil</hi> (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. p. 114), or <hi type="italic">Mshedil</hi> (<hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. p. 143), on the west of <hi type="italic">Mons praecipitii</hi>, though neither of these travellers visited the place, or has given us any minute description of it. Its situation upon a mountain would suit <hi type="italic">Mar'ala</hi>, to which the boundary went up from Sarid. In the case of <hi type="italic">Dabbasheth</hi>, the name, which signifies “lump” (see <reference osisRef="Isa.30.6">Isa 30:6</reference>), points to a mountain. Upon this <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> has founded the conjecture that <hi type="italic">Gibeah</hi> or <hi type="italic">Gibeath</hi> took the place of this uncommon word, and that this is connected with the <hi type="italic">Gabathon</hi> of the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> (<hi type="italic">juxta campum Legionis</hi>), the present <hi type="italic">Jebâta</hi> between Mejeidil and Kaimûn, upon an isolated height on the edge of the mountains which skirt the plain of Jezreel, where there are signs of a remote antiquity (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 201, and Bibl. Res. p. 113; <hi type="italic">Ritter</hi>, Erdk. xvi. p. 700); although Tell <hi type="italic">Thureh</hi> (i.e., mountain) might be intended, a village upon a low and isolated hill a little farther south (see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. p. 116, and <hi type="italic">Ritter, ut sup.</hi>).
entries.511a62063efd834cce855f6c8133b3315c67ebac: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.12">Jos 19:12</reference> <div eID="gen2934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2935" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">And from Sarid the boundary turned eastwards toward the sun-rising to the territory of Chisloth-tabor, and went out to Dabrath, and went up to Japhia</hi>.” <hi type="italic">Chisloth-tabor</hi>, i.e., according to <hi type="italic">Kimchi's</hi> explanation <hi type="italic">lumbi Taboris</hi> (French, <hi type="italic">les flancs</hi>), was at any rate a place on the side of Tabor, possibly the same as <hi type="italic">Kesulloth</hi> in <reference osisRef="Josh.19.18">Jos 19:18</reference>, as <hi type="italic">Masius</hi> and others suppose, and probably the same place as the <hi type="italic">Xaloth</hi> of <hi type="italic">Josephus</hi> (Bell. Jud. iii. 3, 1), which was situated in the “great plain,” and the <hi type="italic">vicus Chasalus</hi> of the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> (<hi type="italic">juxta montem Thabor in campestribus</hi>), i.e., the present village of <hi type="italic">Iksâl</hi> or <hi type="italic">Ksâl</hi>, upon a rocky height on the west of Thabor, with many tombs in the rocks (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 182). <hi type="italic">Dabrath</hi>, a place in the tribe of Issachar that was given up to the Levites (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.28">Jos 21:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.57">1Ch 6:57</reference>), called <hi type="italic">Dabaritta</hi> in <hi type="italic">Josephus</hi> (Bell. Jud. ii. 21, 3) and <hi type="italic">Dabira</hi> in the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> (<hi type="italic">villula in monte Thabor</hi>), the present <hi type="italic">Deburieh</hi>, an insignificant village which stands in a very picturesque manner upon a stratum of rock at the western foot of Tabor (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 210; <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi>, R. ii. p. 324). <hi type="italic">Japhia</hi> certainly cannot be the present <hi type="italic">Hepha</hi> or <hi type="italic">Haifa</hi> (<hi type="italic">Khaifa</hi>) on the Mediterranean, and near to Carmel (Rel. Pal. p. 826, and <hi type="italic">Ges.</hi> Thes. <hi type="italic">s. v.</hi>); but it is just as certain that it cannot be the present <hi type="italic">Jafa</hi>, a place half an hour to the south-west of Nazareth, as <hi type="italic">Robinson</hi> (Pal. iii. p. 200) and <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> suppose, since the boundary was running eastwards, and cannot possibly have turned back again towards the west, and run from Deburieh beyond Sarid. If the positions assigned to Chisloth-tabor and Dabrath are correct, Japhia must be sought for on the east of Deburieh.
entries.db1f9a9558760f34f96ea3be459cbb19527bd005: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.13">Jos 19:13</reference> <div eID="gen2935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2936" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">From thence it went over towards the east to the sun-rising to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin, and went out to Rimmon, which is marked off to Neah</hi>.” <hi type="italic">Gath-hepher</hi>, the home of the prophet Jonah (2Ki 14:25), was “<hi type="italic">haud grandis viculus Geth</hi>” in the time of <hi type="italic">Jerome</hi> (see <hi type="italic">prol. ad Jon.</hi>). It was about two miles from Sephoris on the road to Tiberias, and the tomb of the prophet was shown there. It is the present village of <hi type="italic">Meshed</hi>, a place about an hour and a quarter to the north of Nazareth (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 209; <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi>, Mem. p. 312). <hi type="italic">Eth-kazin</hi> is unknown. <hi type="italic">Rimmon</hi>, a Levitical town (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.35">Jos 21:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.62">1Ch 6:62</reference>), has probably been preserved in the village of <hi type="italic">Rummaneh</hi>, about two hours and a half to the north of Nazareth (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 195). <hi type="italic">Ham-methoar</hi> is not a proper name, but the participle of תּאר, with the article in the place of the relative pronoun, “bounded off,” or pricked off. <hi type="italic">Neah</hi> is unknown; it is possibly the same place as <hi type="italic">Neiel</hi> in the tribe of Asher (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.27">Jos 19:27</reference>), as <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> supposes.
entries.62bc72892a94e5b262f1daa349090575ad0f4447: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.14">Jos 19:14</reference> <div eID="gen2936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2937" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">And the boundary turned round it</hi> (round Rimmon),<hi type="italic">on the north to Channathon, and the outgoings thereof were the valley of Jiphtah-el</hi>.” Judging from the words נסב and מצּפון, this verse apparently gives the north-west boundary, since the last definition in <reference osisRef="Josh.19.13">Jos 19:13</reference>, “to Gath-hepher,” etc., points to the eastern boundary. <hi type="italic">Jiphtah-el</hi> answers no doubt to the present <hi type="italic">Jefât</hi>, two hours and a half to the north of Sefurieh, and is the <hi type="italic">Jotapata</hi> which was obstinately defended by <hi type="italic">Josephus</hi> (Bell. Jud. iii. 7, 9: see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. pp. 104ff.). Consequently the valley of <hi type="italic">Jiphtah-el</hi>, at which Zebulun touched Asher (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.27">Jos 19:27</reference>), is probably “no other than the large Wady Abilîn, which takes its rise in the hills in the neighbourhood of Jefât” (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. p. 107). And if this be correct, <hi type="italic">Channathon</hi> (lxx Ἐνναθώθ) is probably Cana of Galilee, the home of Nathanael (Joh 2:1, Joh 2:11; Joh 4:46; Joh 21:2), the present <hi type="italic">Kana el Jelil</hi>, between Rummaneh and Yefât, on the northern edge of the plain of Buttauf, upon a Tell, from which you overlook the plain, fully two hours and a half in a straight line from Nazareth, and directly north of that place, where there are many ruins found (see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 204; Bibl. Res. p. 108).
entries.0071c79ec7694483b7a519638387224242b92a0d: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.15-Josh.19.16">Jos 19:15-16</reference> <div eID="gen2937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2938" type="x-p"/> The towns of <hi type="italic">Zebulun</hi> were the following. <hi type="italic">Kattath</hi>, probably the same as <hi type="italic">Kitron</hi>, which is mentioned in Jdg 1:30 in connection with Nahalol, but which is still unknown. <hi type="italic">Nehalal</hi>, or <hi type="italic">Nahalol</hi> (Jdg 1:30), is supposed by <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi> (Mem. p. 335), who follows Rabbi <hi type="italic">Schwartz</hi>, to be the present village of <hi type="italic">Maalul</hi>, a place with ruins on the south-west of Nazareth (see <hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. p. 143; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. App.; and <hi type="italic">Ritter</hi>, Erdk. xvi. p. 700). <hi type="italic">Simron</hi> is supposed by <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> to be the village of <hi type="italic">Semunieh</hi> (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.11.1">Jos 11:1</reference>). But neither of these is very probable. <hi type="italic">Idalah</hi> is supposed by <hi type="italic">V. de Velde</hi> to be the village of <hi type="italic">Jeda</hi> or <hi type="italic">Jeida</hi>, on the west of Semunieh, where are a few relics of antiquity, though <hi type="italic">Robinson</hi> (Bibl. Res. p. 113) states the very opposite. <hi type="italic">Bethlehem</hi> (of Zebulun), which many regard as the home of the judge Ibzan (Jdg 12:8), has been preserved under the old name in a miserable village on the north of Jeida and Semunieh (see <hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. p. 139; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. p. 113). The number of the towns is given as <hi type="italic">twelve</hi>, though only five are mentioned by name. It is true that some commentators have found the missing names in the border places mentioned in <reference osisRef="Josh.19.11-Josh.19.14">Jos 19:11-14</reference>, as, after deducting Chisloth-tabor and Dabrath, which belonged to Issachar, the names Sarid, Maralah, Dabbasheth, Japhia, Gittah-hepher, Eth-kazin, and Channathon give just seven towns. Nevertheless there is very little probability in this conjecture. For, in the first place, not only would it be a surprising thing to find the places mentioned as boundaries included among the towns of the territory belonging to the tribe, especially as some of the places so mentioned did not belong to Zebulun at all; but the copula <hi type="italic">vav</hi>, with which the enumeration of the towns commences, is equally surprising, since this is introduced in other cases with הארים והיוּ (ויּהיוּ), e.g., <reference osisRef="Josh.18.21">Jos 18:21</reference>; Jos 15:21. And, in the second place, it is not a probable thing in itself, that, with the exception of the five towns mentioned in <reference osisRef="Josh.19.15">Jos 19:15</reference>, the other towns of Zebulun should all be situated upon the border. And lastly, the towns of <hi type="italic">Kartah</hi> and <hi type="italic">Dimnah</hi>, which Zebulun gave up to the Levites (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.34">Jos 21:34</reference>), are actually wanting. Under these circumstances, it is a natural conclusion that there is a gap in the text here, just as in <reference osisRef="Josh.15.59">Jos 15:59</reference> and Jos 21:36. <div eID="gen2938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2939" type="x-p"/> The Inheritance of Issachar. - In this instance only towns are given, and the boundaries are not delineated, with the exception of the eastern portion of the northern boundary and the boundary line; at the same time, they may easily be traced from the boundaries of the surrounding tribes. Issachar received for the most part the large and very fertile plain of Jezreel (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.17.16">Jos 17:16</reference>, and <hi type="italic">Ritter</hi>, Erdk. xvi. pp. 689ff.), and was bounded on the south by Manasseh, on the west by Manasseh and Asher, on the north by Zebulun, and farther east by Naphtali also, and on the east by the Jordan.
entries.a763ed625164aa75127a7359addfc4101f9a824e: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.18">Jos 19:18</reference> <div eID="gen2939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2940" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">And their boundary was towards Jezreel</hi>,” i.e., their territory extended beyond Jezreel. Jezreel, the summer residence of Ahab and his house (1Ki 18:45-46, etc.), was situated upon a mountain, with an extensive and splendid prospect over the large plain that was called by its name. It was afterwards called <hi type="italic">Esdraela</hi>, a place described in the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> (<hi type="italic">s. v.</hi> <hi type="italic">Jezreel</hi>) as standing between Scythopolis and Legio; it is the present Zerîn, on the north-west of the mountains of Gilboa (see <hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. pp. 155-6; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. pp. 161ff.; <hi type="italic">Van de Velde</hi>, R. ii. pp. 320ff.). <hi type="italic">Chesulloth</hi>, possibly the same as <hi type="italic">Chisloth-tabor</hi> (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.19.12">Jos 19:12</reference>). <hi type="italic">Sunem</hi>, the home of Abishag (1Ki 1:3-15, etc.), also mentioned in <reference osisRef="1Sam.28.4">1Sa 28:4</reference> and 2Ki 4:8, was situated, according to the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi>, five Roman miles (two hours) to the south of Tabor; it is the present <hi type="italic">Solam</hi> or <hi type="italic">Sulem</hi>, at the south-western foot of the Duhy or Little Hermon, an hour and a half to the north of Jezreel (see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. pp. 170ff.; <hi type="italic">Van de Velde</hi>, R. ii. p. 323).
entries.876d958c0021ee1c714d98ccc26dd8ab4370323c: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.19">Jos 19:19</reference> <hi type="italic">Haphraim</hi>, according to the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> (<hi type="italic">s. v.</hi> <hi type="italic">Aphraim</hi>) <hi type="italic">villa Affaraea</hi>, six Roman miles to the north of Legio, is identified by <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> with the village of <hi type="italic">Afuleh</hi>, on the west of Sulem, and more than two hours to the north-east of Legun (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. pp. 163, 181). <hi type="italic">Sion</hi>, according to the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> <hi type="italic">villa juxta montem Thabor</hi>, has not yet been discovered. <hi type="italic">Anaharath</hi> is supposed by <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> to be <hi type="italic">Na'urah</hi>, on the eastern side of the Little Hermon (Bibl. Res. p. 337); but he regards the text as corrupt, and following the <hi type="italic">Cod. Al.</hi> of the lxx, which has Ῥενάθ and Ἀῤῥανέθ, maintains that the reading should be <hi type="italic">Archanath</hi>, to which <hi type="italic">Arâneh</hi> on the north of Jenin in the plain corresponds (<hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. p. 156; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 157). But the circumstance that the <hi type="italic">Cod. Al.</hi> has two names instead of one makes its reading very suspicious.
entries.50d71953b079b0a7c990fa03e3c21e50d5c2205e: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.20">Jos 19:20</reference> <hi type="italic">Harabbit</hi> is supposed by <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> to be <hi type="italic">Araboneh</hi>, on the north-east of Arâneh, at the southern foot of Gilboa (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 157). <hi type="italic">Kishion</hi>, which was given up to the Levites (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.28">Jos 21:28</reference>) and is erroneously written <hi type="italic">Kedesh</hi> in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.57">1Ch 6:57</reference>, is unknown. This also applies to <hi type="italic">Abez</hi> or <hi type="italic">Ebez</hi>, which is never mentioned again.
entries.a27917efc1817d957cdedff9f9ebac5fccb347d3: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.21">Jos 19:21</reference> <hi type="italic">Remeth</hi>, for which <hi type="italic">Jarmuth</hi> stands in the list of Levitical towns in <reference osisRef="Josh.21.29">Jos 21:29</reference>, and <hi type="italic">Ramoth</hi> in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.58">1Ch 6:58</reference>, is also unknown.<note placement="foot"><hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> imagines <hi type="italic">Remeth</hi>, whose name signifies height, to be the village of <hi type="italic">Wezar</hi>, on one of the western peaks of Gilboa (<hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. p. 156; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 166, and Bibl. Res. p. 339), as the name also signifies “a lofty, inaccessible mountain, or a castle situated upon a mountain.” This is certainly not impossible, but it is improbable. For this Mahometan village evidently derived its name from the fact that it has the appearance of a fortification when seen from a distance (see <hi type="italic">Ritter</hi>, Erdk. xv. p. 422). The name has nothing in common therefore with the Hebrew <hi type="italic">Remeth</hi>, and the travellers quoted by him say nothing at all about the ruins which he mentions in connection with <hi type="italic">Wezar</hi> (Wusar).</note><hi type="italic">En-gannim</hi>, which was also allotted to the Levites (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.29">Jos 21:29</reference>; also <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.73">1Ch 6:73</reference>, where it is called <hi type="italic">Anem</hi>), has been associated by <hi type="italic">Robinson</hi> (iii. p. 155) with the Γιναία of <hi type="italic">Josephus</hi>, the present <hi type="italic">Jenin</hi>. The name <hi type="italic">En-gannim</hi> signifies fountain of gardens, and Jenin stands at the southern side of the plain of Jezreel in the midst of gardens and orchards, which are watered by a copious spring (see <hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. pp. 156ff.); “unless perhaps the place referred to is the heap of ruins called <hi type="italic">Um el Ghanim</hi>, on the south-east of Tabor, mentioned by <hi type="italic">Berggren</hi>, ii. p. 240, and <hi type="italic">Van de Velde</hi>, Mem. p. 142” (<hi type="italic">Knobel</hi>). <hi type="italic">En-chadda</hi> and <hi type="italic">Beth-pazzez</hi> are only mentioned here, and have not yet been discovered. According to <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi>, the former of the two may possibly be either the place by Gilboa called <hi type="italic">Judeideh</hi>, with a fountain named <hi type="italic">Ain Judeideh</hi> (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> Bibl. Res. p. 337), or else <hi type="italic">Beit-kad</hi> or <hi type="italic">Kadd</hi> near Gilboa, mentioned by <hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi> (ii. p. 159) and <hi type="italic">Robinson</hi> (iii. p. 157).
entries.46650016eb2c7f3b646bee5b9de359879f32ae50: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.22-Josh.19.23">Jos 19:22-23</reference> <div eID="gen2940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2941" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">And the boundary touched Tabor, Sahazim, and Beth-shemesh</hi>.” <hi type="italic">Tabor</hi> is not the mountain of that name, but a town upon the mountain, which was given to the Levites, though not by Issachar but by Zebulun (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.62">1Ch 6:62</reference>), and was fortified afresh in the Jewish wars (<hi type="italic">Josephus</hi>, Bell. Jud. iv. 1, 8). In this passage, however, it appears to be reckoned as belonging to Issachar, since otherwise there are not sixteen cities named. At the same time, as there are several discrepancies between the numbers given and the names actually mentioned, it is quite possible that in this instance also the number sixteen is incorrect. In any case, Tabor was upon the border of Zebulun (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.12">Jos 19:12</reference>), so that it might have been allotted to this tribe. There are still the remains of old walls and ruins or arches, houses, and other buildings to be seen upon Mount <hi type="italic">Tabor</hi>; and round the summit there are the foundations of a thick wall built of large and to a great extent fluted stones (see <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. pp. 453ff.; <hi type="italic">Seetzen</hi>, ii. p. 148; <hi type="italic">Buckingham</hi>, Syr. i. pp. 83ff.). The places which follow are to be sought for on the east of Tabor towards the Jordan, as the boundary terminated at the Jordan. <hi type="italic">Sachazim</hi> (Shahazimah) <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> connects with <hi type="italic">el Hazetheh</hi>, as the name, which signifies heights, points to a town situated upon hills; and <hi type="italic">el Hezetheh</hi> stands upon the range of hills, bounding the low-lying land of Ard el Hamma, which belonged to Naphtali. The reason is a weak one, though the situation would suit. There is more probability in the conjecture that <hi type="italic">Beth-shemesh</hi>, which remained in the hands of the Canaanites (Jdg 1:33), has been preserved in the ruined village of <hi type="italic">Bessum</hi> (<hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. p. 237), and that this new name is only a corruption of the old one, like <hi type="italic">Beth-shean</hi> and <hi type="italic">Beisan</hi>. It is probable that the eastern portion of the northern boundary of Issachar, towards Naphtali, ran in a north-easterly direction from Tabor through the plain to Kefr Sabt, and thence to the Jordan along the Wady Bessum. It is not stated how far the territory of Issachar ran down the valley of the Jordan (see the remarks on <reference osisRef="Josh.17.11">Jos 17:11</reference>). <div eID="gen2941" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2942" type="x-p"/> The Inheritance of Asher. - Asher received its territory along the Mediterranean Sea from Carmel to the northern boundary of Canaan itself. The description commences with the central portion, viz., the neighbourhood of <hi type="italic">Acco</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.25">Jos 19:25</reference>), going first of all towards the south (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.26">Jos 19:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.27">Jos 19:27</reference>), and then to the north (<reference osisRef="Josh.19.28">Jos 19:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.19.30">Jos 19:30</reference>).
entries.e226c9792c783b2797b943282915edbb19c5b142: <reference osisRef="Josh.19.25">Jos 19:25</reference> <div eID="gen2942" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2943" type="x-p"/> The territory of the Asherites was as follows. <hi type="italic">Helkath</hi>, which was given up to the Levites (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.31">Jos 21:31</reference>, and <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.75">1Ch 6:75</reference>, where <hi type="italic">Hukok</hi> is an old copyist’s error), is the present <hi type="italic">Jelka</hi>, three hours to the east of Acco (Akka: <hi type="italic">Scholz</hi>, Reise, p. 257), or <hi type="italic">Jerka</hi>, a Druse village situated upon an eminence, and judging from the remains, an ancient place (<hi type="italic">Van de Velde</hi>, R. i. p. 214; <hi type="italic">Rob.</hi> iii. App.). <hi type="italic">Hali</hi>, according to <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> possibly <hi type="italic">Julis</hi>, between Jerka and Akka, in which case the present name arose from the form <hi type="italic">Halit</hi>, and <hi type="italic">t</hi> was changed into <hi type="italic">s</hi>. <hi type="italic">Beten</hi>, according to the <hi type="italic">Onom.</hi> (<hi type="italic">s. v.</hi> Βατναι%: <hi type="italic">Bathne</hi>) as <hi type="italic">vicus Bethbeten</hi>, eight Roman miles to the east of Ptolemais, has not yet been found. <hi type="italic">Achshaph</hi> is also unknown (see at <reference osisRef="Josh.11.1">Jos 11:1</reference>).
